body:
Thanks for the contribution! However, I don't understand the connection between #4876, and the diff you've proposed here. In particular, changing "capable of telephone number input" and friends to "layout showing a telephone number input", etc., seems like a regression; it's overly prescriptive.

The way I would address #4876 is to make a small, targeted change, of making none a synonym for text. How does that sound to you?

> Thanks for the contribution! However, I don't understand the connection between #4876, and the diff you've proposed here. In particular, changing "capable of telephone number input" and friends to "layout showing a telephone number input", etc., seems like a regression; it's overly prescriptive.
> 
> The way I would address #4876 is to make a small, targeted change, of making none a synonym for text. How does that sound to you?

Hi @domenic thank you for your feedback!
The the way inputmode value definitions are worded, sounds like there were a directive to control software keyboard invocation. For example, 
> The user agent should display a virtual keyboard...

sounds like it will cause the keyboard to show up. This is why I felt the wording needed to be very precise.

But I won't block on this and if my rationale doesn't justify the change, I will simply address your feedback in the next commit.

> I don't think it's accurate to say we support what's being proposed in this PR. In fact, we'd be opposed to the current PR as it stands.
> 
> When we did the work to make iPad work with desktop sites, it was pretty important for `inputmode=none` to not show virtual keyboard.
> 
> @whsieh

Thank you for your feeddback, @rniwa 

Dependency on `inputmode=none` as a way to prevent virtual keyboard (VK from now on) from showing, seems to me like a misusing the API from what the attribute actually meant to do. 

Reasons:
1. Name `inputmode` implies control over the shape/layout of the keyboard.
2.  Even if number 1 is not obvious, we are conflating two different functionalities in a single API. 

That said, I completely agree with your concerns around compat and not proposing that UAs update the behavior at this very moment. We can keep the behavior for as long as there is continued usage of the `inputmode=none`.
 
Can we agree on the following steps?

1. Consensus on the [new proposal](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CBeWoGxQBpGLXSD2DwfVBf7hmS8Rmxb--Mu9F3Bj24o/edit#heading=h.39l4p2lslcay) and have a html spec PR ready.
2. Once number 1 from above is complete, we update `inputmode=none` with either proposed wording from this PR, or a deprecation note. I think, we would be fine with either one of these approaches.

Thoughts?

inputmode=none was one of the large use cases that motivated this attribute in the first case. GSuite was looking for it I believe to prevent the keyboard from showing up in certain scenarios (Google Slides). Likewise making it dynamic was also part of the design, perhaps I'm biased though because Canada's postal system is ANA NAN for our postal system. (A=alpha, N=numeric) and having the keyboard switch state for an input was a desired property.

@wanderview

> > I don't think it's accurate to say we support what's being proposed in this PR. In fact, we'd be opposed to the current PR as it stands.
> > When we did the work to make iPad work with desktop sites, it was pretty important for `inputmode=none` to not show virtual keyboard.
> > @whsieh
> 
> Thank you for your feeddback, @rniwa
> 
> Dependency on `inputmode=none` as a way to prevent virtual keyboard (VK from now on) from showing, seems to me like a misusing the API from what the attribute actually meant to do.

Well, I think `inputmode` was invented to control the appearance & behavior of software keyboard so I don’t see why it would be a misuse. In fact, the spec today explicitly says it would hide the keyboard so that’s a correct use of the API as far as I read it.

> 1. Name `inputmode` implies control over the shape/layout of the keyboard.

Hiding software keyboard is a mode of control of shape & layout of a software keyboard.

> 2. Even if number 1 is not obvious, we are conflating two different functionalities in a single API.

I don’t agree with that statement. It really depends on how you concepturlize hiding of a keyboard.
 
> That said, I completely agree with your concerns around compat and not proposing that UAs update the behavior at this very moment. We can keep the behavior for as long as there is continued usage of the `inputmode=none`.
> 
> Can we agree on the following steps?
> 
> 1. Consensus on the [new proposal](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CBeWoGxQBpGLXSD2DwfVBf7hmS8Rmxb--Mu9F3Bj24o/edit#heading=h.39l4p2lslcay) and have a html spec PR ready.
> 2. Once number 1 from above is complete, we update `inputmode=none` with either proposed wording from this PR, or a deprecation note. I think, we would be fine with either one of these approaches.

No. I can’t agree with step (2). We shouldn’t be changing the behavior of `inputmode=none` given the current behavior is required for Web compatiblity. Having existing web sites move over to new attribute / behavior is problematic because there will be many people who would be using old devices with old browsers which wouldn’t support such new behaviors.

This ship has already sailed.
